releases.notes:
### 0.129.0

**Echoes read and write like you did**

Your echo now picks up your habits with books. Reading books (from your hand or a lectern) and writing in a book & quill shape how often your echo stops at a chiseled bookshelf or lectern to read, how long it stays with a book, and whether it carries a book & quill around to write in. When it finishes a book it drops it and the book burns away.

- Every book you open makes your echo more likely to stop and read; books you pick up and ditch unread make it less likely
- Long reads give a patient echo; flicking books open and shut gives one that skims
- Writing and signing books makes a writer: it takes a book & quill from a chiseled bookshelf and stops now and then to write, sometimes signing it
- A bookish echo never walks past an open lectern: it stops and reads it there, and never takes the lectern's book
- It reads from chiseled bookshelves and lecterns; even the most bookish echo walks past half the chiseled bookshelves, and it never reads in a fight
- With What Are They Up To installed, a reading or writing echo shows its book panel, just like a player with a book open

releases.notes:
### 0.128.0

**Echoes buy you gifts**

An echo that loves the player it came from now shops for them too. While visiting a trader, if you're nearby, it buys you a piece of armour, a weapon or a tool that beats everything of that kind you own, then walks over and throws it to you. It pays with its own emeralds and junk through the villager's real offers, buys at most one gift a visit, and keeps the gift if you wander off. Echoes trading with villagers now hold up the real villager trading screen.

- Echoes that love you buy you gear that beats what you own and throw it to you
- One gift per visit, paid from the echo's own emeralds and junk at real villager prices
- Echoes now hold up the vanilla villager trading screen while they trade

releases.notes:
### 0.127.0

**Echoes go shopping**

Your echo now shops the way you did. Of the villagers with a job (and wandering traders) you came across in a life, the share you actually traded with becomes your echo's Shopping score, and how long you kept trading screens open becomes how long it lingers. An echo stops at about that share of the traders it walks past, holds up a little trading screen while it sells the junk it has picked up for emeralds, and, once it is keen enough, buys armour, weapons and tools that beat what it is carrying and puts them on. It only ever uses the villager's real offers and stock, and never while it is fighting.

- New Shopping score (0-10) carried from your life to your echo: the share of villagers you met that you traded with
- Late in a long run, walking past villagers counts for less, so marathon runs aren't punished for trading less
- Echoes stop at about that share of the traders they pass, and notice traders from further away the keener they are
- Echoes linger at a trader about as long as you kept trading screens open, holding up a trading screen of their own
- Echoes sell junk to villagers for emeralds; keen shoppers also buy and wear better gear
- Trades use the villager's real prices and stock, and level the villager up like a player trade would
- Wild PlayerMobs and older echoes get a random Shopping score and visit length
- PlayerMobs no longer hoard string as a building block; echoes sell it to fletchers instead

### 0.126.0

**Echoes are slow at what you never did**

An echo is now only quick at the things you actually did quickly in that life. Anything you never did, it does slowly, and a few lucky moments aren't enough to make it sharp. Echoes from lives before echoes learned your reflexes now come back with a reaction speed of their own instead of an average one.

- A skill you never used leaves your echo at its slowest
- Older echoes each get their own reflexes, different every time they return

releases.notes:
### 0.125.0

**Echoes react at your speed for each thing they do**

An echo no longer has one reaction speed for everything. It fights, shoots, builds and moves as quickly as you did each of those things in that life, so a sharp swordsman who fumbled the bow leaves an echo that swings fast but is slow to shoot.

- Shooting speed follows how often your arrows hit and how often you loosed them fully drawn
- Building speed follows how quickly you bridged and pillared
- Anything you never did, your echo does at your usual pace

releases.notes:
### 0.124.0

**Echoes inherit your reflexes**

An echo's reaction speed now comes from how you played that life. Quick hands leave a quick echo, and a slow life leaves a sluggish one. Before this, every echo reacted at the same middling speed.

- Striking back fast, and landing the first hit on something coming for you, count most
- Dodging arrows, keeping your hands busy and pushing on down the train count too
- Quick bridging and pillaring give a small boost

### 0.123.0

**Wild PlayerMobs carry gear like yours**

Naturally spawning PlayerMobs now arrive carrying a random handful of items no better than what the nearest player has: if you are in iron, they can be too, but never in diamond.

- Items are drawn from your best gear tier or anything below it: tools, armour, weapons, materials and food.
- Everything they carry drops when they die.
- Turn it off with naturalSpawnGear=false or /playermob naturalspawngear off.

### 0.121.0

**PlayerMobs dig and build their way to you**

A PlayerMob that can't reach you in a fight no longer just waits. It pillars up, builds steps, tunnels through walls or digs down after you, like a player would.

- Never breaks chests and other storage, unbreakable blocks or train track; the hardest blocks need the right tool
- Keeps hunting you for up to 30 seconds after losing sight of you
- Turn it off with combatReach=false, or with the mobGriefing gamerule

### 0.118.0

**PlayerMobs wear the gear in their backpack, modded gear included**

PlayerMobs now show what they carry. Weapons in a PlayerMob's backpack hang crossed on its back, a shield and banner ride over them, tools hang at its thighs and arrows stick up from a quiver at its shoulder. It works with gear from other mods too: modded swords, tools, bows, crossbows, tridents, shields, banners and arrows show up just like vanilla ones.

- Modded weapons and tools are supported, as long as the mod builds them on Minecraft's own weapon and tool types
- Swords, bows, crossbows, tridents and maces cross on the back
- Shields and banners on the back, pickaxes, axes, shovels and hoes at the thighs
- A quiver shows when it carries arrows
- Turn it off with /playermob carriedgear off or carriedGear=false in config/playermob.properties

### 0.115.0

**Enchantment fix**

Fixed an enchantment not behaving the same on PlayerMobs as it does on players.

### 0.114.0

**No more freezes when a PlayerMob swims for shore**

A PlayerMob that fell into deep water could freeze the whole server for up to a minute while it looked for a bank to climb out on. It now only searches ground the world already has loaded, so the game keeps running and the mob still finds its way back.

- Fixed long server freezes while a PlayerMob swims back to the train

### 0.113.0

**Player Mobs build with proper blocks**

Player Mobs climbing back onto the train no longer build their steps out of beds, doors, torches, slabs or chests. They now only use solid full blocks, and still carry anything else they pick up.

- No more half beds or half doors left beside the track
- Mobs with no suitable blocks gather some or craft planks instead
